claim: Yap1 and Wwtr1 in zebrafish regulates the morphogenesis of the posterior body and epidermal fin fold.
source: In a previous study, it was reported that Yap1 and Wwtr1 in zebrafish regulates the morphogenesis of the posterior body and epidermal fin fold (Kimelman et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kimelman et al., 2017

claim: DNA damage induces apoptosis of epidermal basal cells (EBCs) in zebrafish yap1-/-;wwtr1-/- embryos.
source: We report here that DNA damage induces apoptosis of epidermal basal cells (EBCs) in zebrafish yap1-/-;wwtr1-/- embryos.
evidence: Supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript including TUNEL assays, Caspase activation, and γH2AX staining

claim: Mutant EBCs exhibit active Caspase-3, Caspase-8, and γH2AX.
source: Specifically, these mutant EBCs exhibit active Caspase-3, Caspase-8, and γH2AX, consistent with DNA damage serving as a stimulus of the extrinsic apoptotic pathway in epidermal cells.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4

claim: DNA damage serves as a stimulus of the extrinsic apoptotic pathway in epidermal cells.
source: Specifically, these mutant EBCs exhibit active Caspase-3, Caspase-8, and γH2AX, consistent with DNA damage serving as a stimulus of the extrinsic apoptotic pathway in epidermal cells.
evidence: Inferred from the presence of Caspase-8 activation and γH2AX in mutant cells

claim: Basal cell size growth is inhibited in mutant basal cells followed by apoptosis.
source: Live imaging of zebrafish epidermal cells reveals a steady growth of basal cell size in the developing embryo, but this growth is inhibited in mutant basal cells followed by apoptosis, leading to the hypothesis that factors underscoring cell size play a role in this DNA damage-induced apoptosis phenotype.
evidence: Supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 5 and Video 1

claim: HaCaT cells cultured on stiff substrates exhibit more numerous γH2AX foci compared to ones cultured on soft substrates.
source: We tested two of these factors using cell stretching and substrate stiffness assays, and found that HaCaT cells cultured on stiff substrates exhibit more numerous γH2AX foci compared to ones cultured on soft substrates.
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B

claim: Substrate rigidity may modulate genomic stress in epidermal cells.
source: Thus, our experiments suggest that substrate rigidity may modulate genomic stress in epidermal cells, and that Yap1 and Wwtr1 promotes their survival.
evidence: Based on speculation from experimental observations with HaCaT cells on different substrate stiffnesses

claim: Yap1 and Wwtr1 promote survival of epidermal cells.
source: Thus, our experiments suggest that substrate rigidity may modulate genomic stress in epidermal cells, and that Yap1 and Wwtr1 promotes their survival.
evidence: Supported by data showing increased apoptosis in yap1;wwtr1 mutants and increased γH2AX in knockdown cells

claim: The Hippo signaling pathway is widely known for its role in regulating tissue and organ size.
source: The Hippo signaling pathway is widely known for its role in regulating tissue and organ size (Johnson and Halder, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Johnson and Halder, 2014

claim: Wwtr1 participates in cardiomyocyte decision-making to become a trabecular cell in the developing heart.
source: In the developing heart, Wwtr1 participates in cardiomyocyte decision-making to become a trabecular cell (Lai et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lai et al., 2018

claim: YAP1 and WWTR1 are important for vascular stability.

claim: Yap1 and Wwtr1 regulate kidney branching morphogenesis.

claim: Yap1 and Wwtr1 regulate fibronectin assembly for tail morphogenesis.

claim: Yap1 and Wwtr1 are required for the survival and growth of epidermal cells during skin development.

claim: Genes that are downregulated in yap1;wwtr1 double mutant tailbuds include lama5, col7a1, lamb1a, lamb4, and lamb2, which encode key components of the skin basal lamina.
source: In the transcriptomic signatures from the previous study (Kimelman et al., 2017), genes that are downregulated in yap1;wwtr1 double mutant tailbuds include lama5, col7a1, lamb1a, lamb4, and lamb2, which encode key components of the skin basal lamina.
evidence: Supported by citation to Kimelman et al., 2017

claim: Downregulation of ECM genes likely translates to a different ECM environment in mutant embryos and consequently results in the inhibition of basal cell size.
source: This downregulation likely translates to a different ECM environment in mutant embryos and consequently results in the inhibition of basal cell size (Figure 5).
evidence: Inferred from transcriptomic data and cell size measurements

claim: Yap1 and Wwtr1 likely have important functions in epidermal cell survival and growth during development.
source: Our work reveals that Yap1 and Wwtr1 likely have important functions in epidermal cell survival and growth during development.
evidence: Inferred from all experimental data presented

claim: The yap1bns22 allele was generated from a CRISPR/CAS9-mediated mutagenesis.
source: The yap1bns22 allele was generated from a CRISPR/CAS9-mediated mutagenesis.
evidence: Supported by description in Materials and methods

claim: The yap1bns22 allele contains a 54 bp deletion in the TBD [p.(Pro42_Glu60delinsLeu)].
source: The yap1bns22 allele contains a 54 bp deletion in the TBD [p.(Pro42_Glu60delinsLeu)].
evidence: Supported by description in Materials and methods

claim: Mutant embryos were obtained from an incross of double heterozygous animals.
source: Mutant embryos in this study were obtained from an incross of double heterozygous animals (i.e. yap1bns19/+;wwtr1bns35/+ incross or yap1bns22/+;wwtr1bns35/+ incross).
evidence: Supported by description in Materials and methods

claim: yap1;wwtr1 double mutant embryos older than 16 ss can be visually identified.
source: yap1;wwtr1 double mutant embryos older than 16 ss can be visually identified for experiments.
evidence: Supported by description in Materials and methods

claim: Mechanical perturbations of cells were shown to recruit DNA damage factors including γH2AX and ATR.
source: Mechanical perturbations of cells were shown to recruit DNA damage factors including γH2AX and ATR (Cognart et al., 2020; Kumar et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Cognart et al., 2020; Kumar et al., 2014

claim: The epidermis clears DNA-damaged cells through the extrinsic apoptotic pathway.
source: Previous studies have found that the epidermis clears DNA-damaged cells through the extrinsic apoptotic pathway (Bang et al., 2003; Hill et al., 1999; Takahashi et al., 2001), prompting us to investigate our mutant epidermal cells for DNA damage.
evidence: Supported by citations to Bang et al., 2003; Hill et al., 1999; Takahashi et al., 2001
